summary: Red team of the extraction of Benoist, 'The period-index problem for real surfaces' (Publ. Math. IHÉS 130, 2019), against the published PDF, whose hash matches, and the arXiv v2 TeX. There are 60 findings: six high, 27 medium and 27 low. Most of the 187 items are faithful, but four are false as stated, and the plan has ownership and ordering problems. (1) make_queue merges every accepted Part II by parent and tells the merged job to plan only the first proposal; for the topology and quadratic-form Part IIs the first proposal is an unrelated direction, so the suppliers RealSurfacePeriodIndex imports can be deferred. (2) Route 1 puts Kummer and Brauer sequences that use Pic (SF.3) and the cycle class map (MC.2) into SF.2, closing cycles SF.2→SF.3→SF.2 and SF.2→MC.2→SF.2. (3) Item 141 states Witt's theorem only for unramified classes, which makes Proposition 4.2's use of it circular. (4) Items 75/78 drop Proposition 5.5's hypothesis H¹(R, A|_R) = 0; item 78 is false without it (plane quartic, A = O(1)). (5) The transport step at the end of Proposition 6.6 is unjustified: the integral lift must be normalised before it is carried to nearby fibres (a new source issue). (6) Item 107 claims F₂² stalks; they are Z/4 when 4 ∤ n. Medium findings include: the E3/E4 reasons and their review invert Θ (the paper's Θ is the non-vanishing locus); two conflicting errata records for the same 19 mistakes; new source errors in Lemma 6.4 and Proposition 4.2; items 15 and 118 false in edge cases; no item for the ind ∈ {per, 2per} bound, Artin's comparison, orderings and real closures, or a dozen cited theorems; de Jong's theorem imported from an owner that does not exist; and thirteen duplicates of material already planned elsewhere (Tsen, Serre vanishing, Ehresmann, equivariant cohomology, VHS and Kodaira–Spencer, BW20 and Schröer material). Low findings are locators, misprints, stale notes, and briefs that do not name their imports.

findings.claim: The queue does not plan the four Part IIs under the ids and titles the routes give. paper_designs groups every accepted part-ii route by its parent alone, names the job <base>PartII, drops the route's 'Part II: <what it adds>' title, and tells the design job to plan only the FIRST proposal (registry order) when the proposals split into independent directions, recording a restructure proposal for the rest. For two of Benoist's Part IIs the first proposal is an unrelated direction: DESIGN-AlgebraicTopologyPartII lists Browning–Sawin's 'configurations and rational double loops' first, then BW20 and Benoist's 'involutions and real-locus cohomology'; DESIGN-QuadraticFormInvariantsPartII lists Dittmann–Pop's 'all-characteristic higher Pfister forms' first, then BW20 and Benoist's 'orderings and real function fields'. DESIGN-HodgeStructuresPartII merges seven continuations with Landesman–Litt's 'variations, period maps and non-abelian Hodge theory' first. So the equivariant real-locus topology (29 items here, 49 from BW20) and the ordering/u-invariant theory can legitimately be deferred to a restructure proposal, leaving RealSurfacePeriodIndex without the suppliers its brief imports. The review's claim that the Part IIs merely 'join existing proposals with identical id, parent and title' is checked against the wrong key: the queue ignores the id.

findings.claim: Item 15 ends: 'A Kummer lift's degree-zero fixed-locus component is this characteristic function.' The item is stated for arbitrary α ∈ Br(U), and there the sentence is false. So [α̃ mod 2]_0(x) = (n/2)·α|_x. This is 1_Θ when n ≡ 2 mod 4, but identically 0 when 4 | n, even though Θ can be nonempty.
